§ 01 — Abstract

Project Overview

Transportation networks and waste management systems face major challenges as a result of rapid urbanization. The traditional methods rely on manual procedures and set schedules, which frequently result in inefficiency, service delays, and increased operating expenses. In order to overcome these constraints, this research suggests a model that incorporates Internet of Things (IoT) technologies. The model integrates emergency alert systems, smart bus shelters, and smart waste management into a centralized network infrastructure using Cisco Packet Tracer 8.2. While GPS-enabled buses display real-time arrival information at shelters, smart bins with sensors send fill-level data for the best collection routes. In order to improve employee safety, emergency alert buttons allow for instant incident reporting. With routers, switches, and a central server supporting both static and dynamic IP addressing, the system architecture uses a star topology. According to simulation results, all subsystems have efficient real-time monitoring, dependable communication with 0% packet loss, and an average response time of 43 ms. These results validate the viability of low-cost, IoT-enabled smart town solutions for enhancing efficiency, sustainability, and urban safety.

§ 02 — System Design

Architecture & Components

Three interconnected subsystems managed by a central server over a star topology, all communicating via HTTP with event-driven data updates.

🗑️
Smart Waste Management

Bin sensors periodically transmit fill-level data to the central server. When capacity exceeds 72%, a visual alert fires on the dashboard and a pickup request is logged. Users can submit complaints via a browser-hosted form at complaint.html. Confirmation is sent upon successful submission.

Accuracy: 72%
🚌
Smart Bus Shelter

GPS-enabled buses broadcast location data every 10 seconds. The server calculates ETA using T = d / v and displays it on a Live Bus Tracker page. Example: at 1.5 km distance & 30 km/h speed → ETA = 3 minutes. Data refreshes continuously.

Accuracy: 70%
🚨
Emergency Alert System

Browser-based emergency buttons send HTTP alert packets to the control centre instantly. The server confirms delivery with "Alert Sent Successfully" and a full-screen acknowledgement page. Designed for accidents, health emergencies, and criminal activity in public spaces.

Accuracy: 78%

§ 05 — Conclusion & Future Work

Summary

The proposed smart town simulation demonstrates Cisco Packet Tracer as an affordable, adaptable tool to prototype IoT-enabled urban services before physical deployment, with 75% overall system effectiveness.

✅ Achievements
  • Integrated 3 urban subsystems into a single network
  • 75% overall system effectiveness achieved
  • 0% packet loss — fully reliable simulation link
  • 43ms average response time — sub-50ms latency
  • Browser-accessible dashboards for user interaction
  • Dual IP strategy: static for infra, DHCP for mobile
  • WPA2-PSK AES wireless security implemented
  • Star + hierarchical topology for modular design
⚠️ Limitations
  • Simulation ≠ real-world device heterogeneity
  • Static routing limits adaptive/AI-driven behavior
  • Fault tolerance and energy use not evaluated
  • Scalability untested under heavy traffic loads
  • Vendor interoperability not addressed
  • Long-term sustainability metrics not measured
🚀 Future Directions
  • Integrate ML/AI for demand forecasting and proactive incident response
  • Extend to cloud or edge computing for scalability
  • Add intelligent traffic management & smart lighting
  • Incorporate health monitoring subsystems
  • Deploy on physical hardware for real-world validation
  • Support dynamic routing protocols (OSPF, BGP)
